source.author: ov
source.text: Postquam alta cremata est Ilion et Danaas paverunt Pergama flammas, Naryciusque heros, a virgine virgine rapta, quam meruit poenam solus, digessit in omnes, spargimur et ventis inimica per aequora rapti fulmina, noctem, imbres, iram caelique marisque perpetimur Danai cumulumque Capherea cladis.
source.text_original: Postquam alta cremata est / Ilion et Danaas paverunt Pergama flammas, / Naryciusque heros, a virgine virgine rapta, / quam meruit poenam solus, digessit in omnes, / spargimur et ventis inimica per aequora rapti / fulmina, noctem, imbres, iram caelique marisque / perpetimur Danai cumulumque Capherea cladis.
source.text_english: After lofty Ilion had been burned and Pergama fed the Greek flames, and when the Narycian hero, for the maiden he had raped from the maiden, drew down on all the punishment he alone had deserved, we are scattered and, borne over hostile seas by the winds, we Greeks endure thunderbolts, night, rains, and the wrath of sky and sea, and the crowning disaster of Caphereus.

reuse.author: val
reuse.text: ira maris vastique placent discrimina ponti.
reuse.text_original: ira maris vastique placent discrimina ponti.
reuse.text_english: The wrath of the sea and the perils of the vast deep delight them.
